html:
The Rus' Khaganate is a name some historians give to a possible early state of the Rus in northwest Russia, between about 830 and the 890s. It is on the map for 800, but whether it existed as a state is still argued.

The evidence is thin. In 839 envoys of a people called "Rhos" came with a Byzantine embassy to the court of Louis the Pious; their ruler was called "chacanus", and the Franks found that they were Swedes. Arab writers also describe Rus traders ruled by a khaqan and living on an island. The title khagan was borrowed from the Khazars, the great power of the steppe.

The Rus were Scandinavians, mostly from the lands of the Swedes, who traded furs and slaves for Arab silver along the rivers; see Samanid silver to the Baltic. Suggested centres include Staraya Ladoga and the site near Novgorod. Whatever it was, it came before the state of Kievan Rus'.
sum: The Rus' Khaganate is a name some historians give to a possible early state of the Rus in northwest Russia, between about 830 and the 890s. It is on the map for 800, but whether it existed as a state is still argued.
